page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc5.4xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 6149 processor. Operating at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz, this instance features 16 virtual CPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. The instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance profile. Single-core processing capabilities, including stress-ng single-core CPU tests, Geekbench single-core scores, and single-threaded compression tasks, consistently rank in the bottom 25% of tested servers. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, with stress-ng multi-core, Passmark CPU, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression tests placing in the middle 50%. Memory bandwidth tests also demonstrate average throughput, reaching 73.32 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 38.81 GB/sec for write operations.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.hfc5.4xlarge is its weak single-threaded execution speed relative to its multi-threaded capacity. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers a balanced compute-to-RAM ratio of 1:2, making it suitable for multi-threaded workloads that do not require high per-core performance or massive memory footprints. Appropriate workloads include static web serving, Redis database operations, software compilation, and light multi-threaded batch processing. It is less suited for single-threaded applications or medium-to-large language model inference.
